stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple has reportedly delayed its first smart glasses from an early-2027 target to a June 2027 unveiling, with sales expected by year-end, as it works on privacy safeguards and how to explain them. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple plans to emphasize on-device processing, no facial recognition and no use of customer recordings for AI training, a sharp contrast with concerns over covert recording by rival Meta glasses.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A small but growing group of Democrats is adopting “America First” language to oppose U.S. involvement in the Iran war and argue for spending more at home. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, California Rep. Ro Khanna and Nebraska independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn are among those using the phrase, Axios reports, showing how Trump’s signature slogan is being contested as the conflict reshapes both parties’ politics.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Democratic National Committee panel voted Friday to open the 2028 presidential primary season in South Carolina, angering progressives who believe the choice favors the party establishment. Bernie Sanders lost South Carolina decisively in both 2016 and 2020, while he won Nevada in 2020, the alternative state that narrowly lost the first-place slot. The dispute adds to Democrats’ broader clash over left-wing challengers and centrist candidates before the 2026 midterms.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques and also targeted cars and farmland in West Bank villages, Palestinian officials said, following a deadly confrontation near Tal two days earlier. That clash killed four Palestinians and two Israelis, with each side blaming the other; Israel’s military said troops were sent to Qusra and police would gather evidence. The reported attacks deepen an already escalating cycle of settler and Palestinian violence in the occupied territory.

stories.delivered_paragraph: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged “unwavering” support for Ukraine before hosting President Volodymyr Zelensky, his first international visitor since taking office a week ago. At a naval base, Burnham is due to offer Ukraine the intellectual property for Britain’s tablet-sized Stone Cloak drone-jamming system, thousands of which the Ministry of Defence has already supplied. The arrangement would let Ukraine manufacture the frontline-tested technology at scale.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MLB contenders are weighing roster upgrades ahead of the Aug. 3 trade deadline at 6 p.m. ET, with Detroit ace Tarik Skubal and Boston closer Aroldis Chapman among the most closely watched names. stories.delivered_paragraph: Charli xcx released a $4.99 digital deluxe edition of “Music, Fashion, Film” on iTunes, making three previously physical-only B-sides officially available for download. The edition adds “I Keep On Thinking Bout You Every Single Day and Night,” “Playboy Bunny” and “If You Take the Music Then What Has She Got?” to the album’s 11 original tracks, along with their videos. It reverses her earlier suggestion that the songs would not reach streaming or digital platforms.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Tadej Pogačar won his fifth Tour de France, tying the record held by Eddy Merckx, Miguel Indurain, Bernard Hinault and Jacques Anquetil. The 27-year-old Slovenian seized the yellow jersey on Stage 6 and held it through the final 15 stages, finishing 6 minutes 26 seconds ahead despite rival Jonas Vingegaard’s Stage 15 collarbone crash. Pogačar is now the youngest five-time winner and has a chance to claim the record outright.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Verge argues that John De Hart’s “Champagne and Bullets” deserves a place alongside cult “so-bad-they’re-good” films such as “The Room” and “Troll 2.” De Hart wrote, directed and stars in the movie, also released as “GetEven” and “Road to Revenge,” whose awkward performances and baffling character interactions are central to its appeal. The review positions the film as an outsider-cinema curiosity rather than a conventionally successful action movie.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Marvel chief Kevin Feige said director Ryan Coogler chose David Jonsson for the next “Black Panther” after a secret hotel meeting about six months ago, before the studio had begun a formal casting search. Coogler, then focused on “Sinners,” told Feige Jonsson was “the guy” after seeing his work and meeting him; Feige said the call gave him chills. The account signals that the franchise’s next lead has been selected as development on “Black Panther 3” advances.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Apple will report earnings in the busiest week of the summer reporting season, while the Federal Reserve’s July meeting gives investors another major market test. Boeing reports Tuesday after its shares were pressured by renewed Middle East tensions and higher oil prices, CNBC notes. Results from the large technology companies and the Fed’s policy signals will help determine whether recent market moves extend or reverse.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Oil prices fell and U.S. stock-index futures rose Sunday after the United States and Iran paused attacks, easing investors’ immediate concern that the conflict would disrupt energy supplies. The relief rally comes before a Federal Reserve meeting and earnings from major technology companies, both of which could quickly redirect trading. Markets remain sensitive to whether the pause in fighting holds and to what corporate results say about the economy.
